<n>6</n> Qui ait ei: Ecce vir Dei est in civitáte hac, vir nóbilis: omne quod lóquitur, sine ambiguitáte venit; nunc ergo eámus illuc, si forte índicet nobis de via nostra, propter quam vénimus.
<n>7</n> Dixítque Saul ad púerum suum: Ecce íbimus: quid ferémus ad virum Dei? panis defécit in sitárciis nostris, et spórtulam non habémus, ut demus hómini Dei, nec quidquam áliud.

b.2ff459ebd0:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uinto Idus Iúnii Luna quinta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>N</h>oménti, in Sabínis, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Primi et Feliciáni fratrum, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Imperatóribus. Hi gloriósi Mártyres, cum longǽvam in Dómino vitam duxíssent, et nunc simul pária, nunc singillátim divérsa et exquisíta pertulíssent torménta, ambo tandem felícis pugnæ cursum, a Nomentáno Prǽside Promóto animadvérsi gládio, consummavérunt. Ipsórum autem Mártyrum córpora, póstea Romam transláta, in Ecclésia sancti Stéphani Protomártyris, in monte Cǽlio, honorífice collocáta sunt.
<h>A</h>génni, in Gállia, pássio sancti Vincéntii, Levítæ et Mártyris, qui, ob Christi fidem, verbéribus diríssime cæsus et gládio decollátus est.
<h>A</h>pud Antiochíam sanctæ Pelágiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quam sancti Ambrósius et Joánnes Chrysostómus magnis éfferunt láudibus.
<h>S</h>yracúsis, in Sicília, sancti Maximiáni Epíscopi, cujus sanctus Gregórius Papa sǽpius méminit.
<h>A</h>ndriæ, in Apúlia, sancti Richárdi, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, et miráculis cláruit.
<h>I</h>n Jóna, Scótiæ ínsula, sancti Colúmbæ, Presbýteri et Abbátis.
<h>E</h>déssæ, in Sýria, sancti Iuliáni Mónachi, cujus præclára gesta sanctus Ephræm Diáconus scripsit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.a293f23d09:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 9th 2027, the 5th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>U</h>pon the Celian Mount of Rome, the holy Martyrs Primus and Felician, who suffered under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian. These glorious martyrs had led a long life together, and had suffered diverse and dreadful torments sometimes together, and sometimes apart. At length they brought their happy fight to a close, being beheaded under Promotus, President of Mentana.
<h>A</h>t Agen, in Gaul, [in the third century,] suffered the holy martyr Vincent the Levite.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, [in the year 304,] the holy Virgin martyr Pelagia, whom holy Ambrose and John Chrysostom do greatly praise.
<h>A</h>t Syracuse, [in the year 594,] holy Maximian, Bishop [of that see,] of whom holy Pope Gregory the Great doth oftentimes make mention.
<h>A</h>t Andria, in Apulia, [in the twelfth century,] holy Richard, the first Bishop of that city, famous for wondrous works.
<h>I</h>n Scotland, [in the year 597,] holy Colum, Priest and Confessor, [founder and first Abbot of Jona.]
<h>A</h>t Edessa, in Syria, [in the fourth century,] the holy monk Julian, whose illustrious acts are written by the holy Deacon Ephraim.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.df7fa85889:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>rotéctor in te sperántium, Deus, sine quo nihil est válidum, nihil sanctum; multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, te rectóre, te duce, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.113b36730a:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, the protector of all them that trust in thee, without whom nothing is strong, nothing is holy; increase and multiply upon us thy mercy, that thou being our ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we finally lose not the things eternal.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
